source_text: Delectat prorsus et penitus afficit, causari imbecillitatem naturae, dicere carnem congenitis obnoxiam esse peccatis, nec in voluntate hominis emendationis effectum locare, sed studiorum crimina officia vocare membrorum; catholicam hanc fidem esse, ut liberum confiteatur arbitrium, sed per quod homo malum facere cogatur, bonum velle non possit.
pass_a_gloss: It altogether delights and inwardly affects them to plead the weakness of nature, to say that the flesh is liable to inborn sins, and not to place the effect of amendment in the will of a human being, but to call the crimes of pursuits the functions of the members; that this is the catholic faith, that it confess a free decision, but one through which a human being is compelled to do evil and cannot will the good.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: They positively delight in—and are deeply attached to—pleading nature’s weakness, saying that the flesh is subject to sins from birth, and placing the achievement of reform outside the human will. They call the crimes of deliberate conduct the functions of bodily parts. They say that the catholic faith consists in confessing a free will, but one through which a person is compelled to do evil and cannot will the good.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
